text:
The Bruins' five-game winning streak ended in Dallas two days ago, a 3-2 overtime loss in which Mikko Rantanen scored three goals. They are still 4-0-1 in their last five and have points in six straight. The Predators, off four days of rest, snapped a three-game winless run by beating STL 5-2 last Saturday. Mavrik Bourque is off the out list and day-to-day.

Boston's results run ahead of its play. The Bruins hold a +14 goal difference on a -1.4 expected one (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and finishing and goaltending are doing the lifting. Nashville has taken 45% of the expected goals at five on five to Boston's 51%. The model projects 2.96 goals for BOS and 2.78 for NSH. Boston takes 4.6 penalties a game, which hands the other side power plays, though Nashville's power play is at 0.62 expected goals a game to the Bruins' 0.47.

The goalie matchup favors the home side. Projected starter Jeremy Swayman is at +7.7 goals saved above expected this season (+26.5 last year) and has a .936 save percentage over his last five starts. Juuse Saros sits at +1.5 this season after a -10.2 mark last year.

Watch David Pastrnak, who has a 32% chance to score and a 76% chance at a point, and who runs the Bruins' top power play. Matthew Poitras has 6 points in his last seven games, and the chances he's getting back it up. For Nashville, Steven Stamkos (35% to score) leads the model's picks, with Filip Forsberg (34%) close behind.
